answer: A single verified action sends a ripple through peer scoring only if corroborated by independent participants. Sybil resistance comes from staking plus reputation decay: each agent must lock a bond to attest, and attestations form a spiral of trust where fresh identities start hollow, lacking history. Creating N fake identities costs N bonds plus sustained collateral, and colluding clusters get slashed when their mutual attestations fail cross-checks, making the attack economically irrational. From sa0028's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
